rows.description: Feeling cornered before an audience, the child drags in old grievances and insults the friend's family or looks. Winning starts to matter more than the swing, and the words chosen are meant to hurt.
graph_context: previous stage: Blame and counter-blame
next stage: Flooding
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: grief, hurt

rows.subtype: Stage 6: Owning your part, not the whole [Response]
rows.description: Each says what they regret without demanding the other apologise first. A mature repair keeps friendship above who started it, and the group cools when the two of them do.
graph_context: previous stage: One person moves first
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22
related mind states: regret

rows.subtype: Stage 6: Repair and one concrete agreement [Response]
rows.description: On returning, each restates the other's point before their own and owns their harshest words. They leave with one small practical agreement, like a rota, because a shared plan holds better than a shared feeling.
graph_context: previous stage: Calling a time-out
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: She feels invisible and powerless, tries everything from questions to tears, then goes cold herself. Being shut out touches old fears of not mattering, and hurt often turns into anger.
graph_context: previous stage: Stonewalling becomes a habit
next stage: Mutual freeze
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: anger, fear, hurt

rows.description: A child grabs a friend's toy and the friend cries. The child feels a flicker of wanting and then confusion at the crying, and may freeze, laugh nervously or say "I did not do it".
graph_context: next stage: Notice the other's feelings
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: amusement, sadness, anxiety, confusion

rows.description: The teacher crouches down and points to what is visible: "Look, Aman is sad, his face is wet." She helps the child link his action to his friend's tears, which is empathy being built.
graph_context: previous stage: The harm happens
next stage: Defensiveness
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: sadness, empathy

rows.description: The mother says "I am hurt by the lie, and I also want to know why you felt you could not ask me." The teen admits fear of being refused, and both hear something they did not expect.
graph_context: previous stage: Punishment and defensiveness
next stage: A clear path back
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: fear, hurt

rows.description: Two children seated together discover they both like cricket cards and start trading. Friendship at this age grows from sharing a bench, a game or a joke, more than from deep knowledge of each other.
graph_context: next stage: Testing safety
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: interest

rows.description: A toddler is told it is time to leave the park. He cannot manage the wish to stay, so his face crumples, his body stiffens and he starts to cry.
graph_context: next stage: Peak of the storm
this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6
related mind states: sadness, anger

rows.description: He drops to the floor, screams, kicks and may throw things or arch his back. He cannot listen or reason, since the brain areas for calming are still very immature.
graph_context: previous stage: Trigger and frustration
next stage: Caregiver's stress and choice point
this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6
related mind states: calm
